# Per-workspace image source: global recipe, own recipe (built on save) or ready-made image

## What to build

A graph-manager workspace can now pick where its sandbox image comes from. There are three **sources**:

- **`global`** (the default): the image built from the global recipe in `sandboxRecipe`.
- **`recipe`**: the workspace's own full copy of a recipe (`{ base, toolchains, extraLines }`), with its own Node base image. Its image is built when the settings are saved.
- **`image`**: a ready-made image name (the existing escape hatch), used as is.

This slice is server only:
- the store shape
- the per-workspace build state, with one build at a time
- image selection and the 409/400 answers in `Sandboxes.start()`
- the workspace settings and build routes
- cleanup that keeps every recipe's image

Another slice does the workspace drawer UI. Don't touch `src/web` beyond what `npm run typecheck` forces; if `src/web/types.ts` needs nothing, leave it.

The recipe model already exists in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox-image.ts`:
- `SandboxRecipe { base; toolchains: { id, enabled, snippet }[]; extraLines }`
- `TOOLCHAINS`, `DEFAULT_RECIPE` and `defaultRecipe(config)` (a deep copy, with `GM_SANDBOX_IMAGE` as base)
- `recipeSchema` (zod, strict) and `migrateRecipe(raw)`, which converts the old `{ base, packages, extraLines }`
- `normalizeRecipe(r)` and `validateRecipe(r)`, which returns a 400 message or undefined
- `sandboxDockerfile(r)`, `sandboxImageTag(dockerfile)` (`gm-sandbox:<12 hex>`), `ensureSandboxImage(docker, recipe, { force, onLine })`, `ensureCliImage`, `ensureClisVolume`, and `removeOldImages(docker, keepIds)`

The global recipe already works: `GET/PUT /api/settings/sandbox`, `POST /api/sandbox/dockerfile` and `POST /api/sandbox/rebuild`.

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox.ts`, all of it (about 670 lines). In particular:
  - lines 49–72: `SandboxStatus` and `SandboxBuild`, whose state gains `"queued"`
  - lines 134–160: private fields (`build`, `building`, `preparing`, `forceNext`, `clisVolume`, `image`)
  - lines 177–300: `status()`, `isBuilding()`, `rebuild()`, `buildState()`, `ensureImages()`, `buildImages()`, `recipe()`, `defaultImage()` and `canBuild()`
  - lines 326–360: the start of `start()`, which does image selection at line 333 (`p.image || store.get().workspaceSettings[p.ws.id]?.image || this.defaultImage()`), rebuilds a missing built image at lines 335–340, then pulls or inspects
  - lines 607–672: `doInit()` and `imagesStatus()`
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/store.ts`, lines 60–70: `workspaceSettings: z.record(z.string(), z.object({ image: z.string().optional(), sandbox: z.boolean().optional() }))`.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/sandbox.ts`, lines 70–98: `view()` and `GET/PUT /api/workspaces/:id/settings` (`wsSettingsBody = z.object({ image: z.string().trim().max(255).nullable() }).strict()`, with `resolveWorkspace(ctx.config.workspacesDir, id)` answering 404).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/runs.ts`, lines 50–60 and 110–125: how the start route saves `workspaceSettings[id].sandbox` and turns a `SandboxError` into its HTTP status. `routes/internal.ts` (around line 110) and `routes/resume.ts` (line 52) call `sandboxes.start` too, and need no change.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox-image.test.ts`, lines 196–325: the `Sandboxes image build` tests:
  - `fake({ buildDelayMs })`, `sandboxes(f)`, the `until(label, fn)` helper and `params`
  - asserting `f.builds` (`{ tag, nocache, labels, dockerfile }`)
  - `prepareTools` mocked in `beforeEach`
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/sandbox.test.ts`, lines 253–306: the workspace settings route tests (`withWorkspace()`, `settings(c, method, payload, id, cookie)`).
- `apps/graph-manager/scripts/fake-docker.mjs`, lines 589–610: a Dockerfile containing `FAKE_BUILD_FAIL` fails its build; `--build-delay`/`buildDelayMs` slows builds.

## Patterns to follow

**Store** (`store.ts`):

```ts
workspaceSettings: z.record(z.string(), z.object({
  image: z.string().optional(),
  sandbox: z.boolean().optional(),
  recipe: z.preprocess(migrateRecipe, recipeSchema).optional(),
})).default({}),
```

- At most one of `image` and `recipe` is set. With neither, the source is `global`.

**Image selection** (new public methods on `Sandboxes`):

```ts
/** The image source of a workspace and its image. */
imageFor(wsId: string): { source: "global" | "recipe" | "image"; image: string } {
  const s = this.opts.store.get().workspaceSettings[wsId];
  if (s?.image) return { source: "image", image: s.image };
  if (s?.recipe) return { source: "recipe", image: sandboxImageTag(sandboxDockerfile(s.recipe)) };
  return { source: "global", image: this.defaultImage() };
}
```

**Builds and the queue**:
- **Per-target state**: keep the global build as it is (`this.build`, `ensureImages`, `rebuild`, `status()`). Add a per-workspace state, `private readonly wsBuilds = new Map<string, SandboxBuild>()`, and `wsBuildState(wsId): SandboxBuild`, which returns a copy or `{ state: "idle", log: [] }`.
- **One build at a time**: add a private promise chain, for example `private queue: Promise<unknown> = Promise.resolve()`, and a helper `private serial<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>` that appends to it and never lets a rejection break the chain.
  - The global `buildImages` call inside `ensureImages` goes through `serial` too.
  - Workspace builds go through `serial`.
  - While a target waits in the chain its state is `"queued"`, and it becomes `"building"` when it starts.
- **`queueWorkspaceBuild(wsId, { force? } = {}): void`**:
  - Does nothing when that workspace's state is already `queued` or `building`, or when its source isn't `recipe`.
  - Otherwise it sets `{ state: "queued", log: [] }` and runs `serial(async () => …)`. Inside: state `building`, `step: "clis"`. If `this.clisVolume` is unset, call `ensureCliImage(this.docker, GM_VERSION, { onLine })` and then `ensureClisVolume`, and set `this.clisVolume`. Then `step: "image"` and `ensureSandboxImage(this.docker, <the recipe read from the store at that moment>, { force, onLine })`. Then `ready` and `finishedAt`, and run the cleanup below.
  - Errors set `state: "failed"` and `error: messageOf(err)`, and never reject.
  - Logs keep at most 1000 lines, like `ensureImages` (`BUILD_LOG_LINES`).
- **Cleanup**: replace the `removeOldImages(this.docker, [cli.id, sb.id])` call in `buildImages` with a helper `private async keepIds(): Promise<string[]>`. It inspects the CLI image tag, the global recipe's tag and every workspace recipe's tag, ignoring missing ones, and returns their ids.
  - Call `removeOldImages(this.docker, await this.keepIds())` after every successful global or workspace build.
  - Keep the gm-clis volume cleanup as it is.
- **At startup**: at the end of a successful global build (in `ensureImages`' success branch), queue the build of every workspace whose source is `recipe` and whose image doesn't exist (`docker.inspectImage(tag)` is undefined). Don't queue workspaces whose last build failed.

**`start()` changes** (replace line 333 and the missing-image block):
- **Pick the image**: `const sel = p.image ? { source: "image", image: p.image } : this.imageFor(p.ws.id)`.
- **Recipe source**: check these before the global `isBuilding()` / `status()` checks for that workspace. A recipe workspace must not wait for the *global* image build, but it still needs the tools (`toolsMount`) and the CLI volume (`clisMount`).
  - If the workspace build state is `queued` or `building`, throw `new SandboxError(409, "the sandbox image of this workspace is building; try again when it is ready")`.
  - If the state is `failed`, throw `new SandboxError(400, \`the sandbox image build failed: ${error}\`)`.
  - If the image doesn't exist (`docker.imageExists(sel.image)` is false), `queueWorkspaceBuild(p.ws.id)` and throw the same 409. Never pull a `gm-sandbox:` image.
  - Docker must still be available (`status()` not failing for reasons other than the global build). Keep the 400 for "Docker is not reachable".
- **Global and image sources**: unchanged.
- The CLI volume mount (`clisMount()`) is used for every source. If it is missing for a recipe workspace, throw the same 409 (the CLI image is still building).

**Routes** (`routes/sandbox.ts`):
- **View**: `const view = (id) => ({ sandbox, source, image: s?.image ?? null, recipe: s?.recipe ?? null, dockerfile: s?.recipe ? sandboxDockerfile(s.recipe) : null, effectiveImage: ctx.sandboxes?.imageFor(id).image ?? <the global tag> })`.
- **`PUT /api/workspaces/:id/settings` body**: `z.union` of
  - `z.object({ source: z.literal("global") }).strict()`
  - `z.object({ source: z.literal("image"), image: z.string().trim().max(255) }).strict()`
  - `z.object({ source: z.literal("recipe"), recipe: recipeSchema }).strict()`
  - and the old `z.object({ image: z.string().trim().max(255).nullable() }).strict()`, where a non-empty string means `image` and null or empty means `global`
- **Errors**:
  - an invalid image gives 400 `{ error: "image: not a valid image reference" }`, as today
  - an invalid recipe gives 400 `{ error: validateRecipe(...) }`
  - a recipe save whose Dockerfile changed while that workspace's build is queued or building gives 409 `{ error: "the sandbox image of this workspace is building; try again when it is ready" }`
- **Saving**: set exactly one of `image` / `recipe` (store `normalizeRecipe(recipe)`), delete the other, and keep `sandbox`.
  - After saving a recipe whose image doesn't exist, call `ctx.sandboxes?.queueWorkspaceBuild(ws.id)`. Saving after a failed build always queues, so the user can retry by saving.
  - Answer `view(ws.id)` plus `build: wsBuildState(ws.id)`.
- **`GET /api/workspaces/:id/sandbox/build`**: answers `wsBuildState(id)`, with 404 for an unknown workspace.
- **`POST /api/workspaces/:id/sandbox/rebuild`**:
  - 400 `{ error: "the workspace has no own recipe" }` unless the source is `recipe`
  - 409 while queued or building
  - otherwise `queueWorkspaceBuild(id, { force: true })` and 202 `{ build }`
- `PUT /api/workspaces/:id/settings` and `GET /api/sandbox/status` keep requiring login, as all `/api` routes do.

## Step-by-step tasks

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/store.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: the `recipe` field above. Import `migrateRecipe` and `recipeSchema` from `./sandbox-image.js`.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - `SandboxBuild.state` gains `"queued"`.
  - Add `imageFor`, `wsBuildState`, `queueWorkspaceBuild`, `serial` and `keepIds`, the startup queueing, and the `start()` changes.
- **GOTCHA**:
  - Don't change the global behaviour the existing tests check: init answers `building` at once, a start during the global build is 409, Rebuild forces both images, and a failed global build doesn't rebuild by itself.
  - `status()` stays about the global image only.
  - The fake Docker gives each build a new image id. `removeOldImages` must keep the ids of every recipe image, or a workspace image would be deleted after the next global build.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/sandbox.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: the routes above.

### UPDATE the tests

**`sandbox-image.test.ts`**, new `describe("workspace recipes")`:
1. A workspace with its own recipe (java enabled, base `node:22-bookworm`), queued with `queueWorkspaceBuild`, builds `gm-sandbox:<hash of its Dockerfile>` after the global build.
   - Its state goes `queued` → `building` → `ready`.
   - `f.builds` holds each tag once.
   - `imageFor(ws).image` is that tag.
2. While it is building (`buildDelayMs: 1500`), `start()` for that workspace throws 409 with the exact message, and `start()` for another workspace on `global` doesn't throw that 409.
   - Use `fake({ exec: false })`. A start that gets past image selection may fail later for other reasons; assert only that it isn't the workspace 409.
3. With `RUN echo FAKE_BUILD_FAIL` in the extra lines, the state becomes `failed`, and `start()` throws 400 `the sandbox image build failed: …`.
4. After a second global build, the workspace image still exists (`docker.inspectImage(tag)` is defined), while an image of a recipe no workspace uses any more is removed.
5. On init with a workspace recipe whose image is missing, the workspace build is queued after the global one.
6. Two queued targets never build at the same time. With `buildDelayMs`, record start and end times through `onLine`, or assert `f.builds` order and that the second starts after the first's state is no longer `building`.

**`routes/sandbox.test.ts`**:
- `GET` on a new workspace answers `{ sandbox: false, source: "global", image: null, recipe: null, dockerfile: null, effectiveImage: <global tag> }`.
- `PUT { source: "recipe", recipe }` stores it, answers `source: "recipe"`, a `dockerfile` starting with `FROM node:22-bookworm` and a `build.state` of `queued` or `building`, and `GET …/sandbox/build` follows it.
- `PUT { source: "image", image: "python:3.12-bookworm" }` clears the recipe.
- `PUT { source: "global" }` clears both and keeps `sandbox: true`.
- The old `{ image }` and `{ image: null }` bodies still work, so keep the existing tests passing with the new response shape.
- An invalid recipe gives 400, `POST …/sandbox/rebuild` on a global workspace gives 400, an unknown workspace gives 404, and no login gives 401.

**`routes/runs.sandbox.test.ts`**: add one case where a sandboxed start in a workspace whose own recipe is building answers 409 with the message.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `PUT /api/workspaces/:id/settings` with `{ source: "recipe", recipe }` saves the recipe, clears `image`, and queues that workspace's build, which `GET /api/workspaces/:id/sandbox/build` shows as `queued` / `building` and then `ready`.
- [ ] While it builds, `POST /api/runs/<that workspace>` with `sandbox: true` answers 409 `the sandbox image of this workspace is building; try again when it is ready`; other workspaces aren't blocked by it.
- [ ] After the build, that workspace's container uses `gm-sandbox:<hash of its own Dockerfile>`, with `/opt/gm-clis` mounted; other workspaces use the global image.
- [ ] A workspace with `source: "image"` uses that image (pulled when missing), with `/opt/gm-clis` mounted.
- [ ] A failed workspace build gives 400 `the sandbox image build failed: …` on start; saving again or `POST …/sandbox/rebuild` retries.
- [ ] Builds run one at a time; cleanup keeps the CLI image, the global image and every workspace recipe's image.
- [ ] The old `{ image: string | null }` body still works.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test -w graph-manager` pass.

## Validation commands

```bash
npm run typecheck && npm run lint
npm test -w graph-manager -- src/server/sandbox-image.test.ts src/server/routes/sandbox.test.ts src/server/routes/runs.sandbox.test.ts src/server/sandbox.test.ts
npm test -w graph-manager
```
